situation:
You are a young adult moving out of a parent's home for the first time, into an apartment you will share with one roommate. A financial coach (judge) at CEDAR FORK COMMUNITY FINANCE CENTER has agreed to meet with you and hear how you plan to handle your first paychecks.

The lease requires a security deposit and the first month's rent, nine hundred dollars together, within six weeks. You have exactly that much saved, sitting in the checking account you opened at PIONEER STATE BANK, and its fee schedule waives the monthly maintenance charge only in months a direct deposit lands.

The full-time job you start next week matches retirement contributions dollar for dollar, but only on money withheld from a paycheck. You also owe a completed Form W-4 before your first payday.

You could set the retirement contribution to zero for now and keep the nine hundred dollars whole. The lease gets signed on time, and every month you skip is a month of the dollar-for-dollar match you never get back.

You could instead contribute enough to earn the full match and cover the deposit by having less tax withheld on the Form W-4. Both goals stay alive, and a smaller amount withheld can leave you owing tax next April, with no money set aside to pay it.

The coach (judge) wants you to compare what each course costs and recommend one. The coach (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after you have presented and answered the questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of a financial coach (judge) at CEDAR FORK COMMUNITY FINANCE CENTER.

Background is the same as the situation above. The lease requires nine hundred dollars in deposit and first month's rent within six weeks, that is exactly what is saved, the new full-time job matches retirement contributions dollar for dollar only on money withheld from a paycheck, and a Form W-4 is due before the first payday.

You have asked the participant to compare what each course costs and recommend one.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how would you know this was the right call?
What would you look at to tell whether the W-4 was filled in correctly?
